page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v5 is a high-vCPU virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. The server is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz, comprising 48 physical cores and 96 virtual processors via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is configured at 192.0 GB total, yielding a compute-leaning 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor incorporates 48 MB of Level 3 cache, 1 MB of Level 2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance operates without bundled local SSD storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results highlight substantial parallel compute throughput, placing the instance in the upper 25 percent tier for multi-core stress testing and Geekbench multi-core performance (17,853.0 points). Clang software compilation benchmarks score 55,284.0, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression processes at 428.41 GB/sec. The integration of advanced cryptographic instructions results in top-decile performance on the PassMark encryption test at 87,240.76. In contrast, single-thread evaluations across Geekbench (1701.0) and single-core stress-ng reflect median performance typical of standard 2.8 GHz base clocks. Large-block memory bandwidth exhibits high throughput, registering 329.31 GB/sec read and 140.95 GB/sec write.

Architecturally, the reduced memory footprint of 2.0 GB per core improves cost efficiency for environments where high thread density is mandatory but massive per-thread memory pools remain underutilized. Rather than paying for surplus memory allocations common in standard 1:4 memory-to-core ratios, this configuration minimizes idle RAM overhead. The primary tradeoff stems from the complete absence of local ephemeral scratch space, which necessitates provisioning remote block storage for all filesystem I/O, alongside moderate single-core speeds that limit utility for single-threaded bottlenecks.

The D96ls_v5 is best suited for compute-bound parallel workloads that do not demand extensive memory arrays. These include continuous integration build farms, parallel software compilation, batch ETL data pipelines, high-concurrency static web serving (benchmarked at 63.95 GB/sec throughput), and SSL/TLS or cryptographic proxying services capable of leveraging Intel VAES acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v5 is a compute-focused general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Configured with a lean 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, the instance totals 192.0 GB of system RAM, omitting local storage and hardware GPU acceleration in favor of remote storage attachments. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier encryption execution driven by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instructions, alongside upper-quartile multi-threaded performance in PassMark, multi-core stress testing, and Clang compilation tasks. Single-thread processing registers within median thresholds, reflecting standard base clock rates. The balanced 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes high core density without the overhead of surplus unallocated RAM, positioning the server as an efficient deployment target for multi-threaded build farms, continuous integration pipelines, batch data transforms, static web serving fleets, and network security appliances requiring heavy cryptographic throughput.
